title: AI found two critical holes in PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites, and the patches are out: update now
summary: PHP’s maintainers shipped PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 on October 21 to fix two critical flaws that can let an attacker run code on a web server without logging in. Security firm Calif found one using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol as part of OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, and Wiz Research independently found both, using its Wiz Atlas agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz, which calls the bugs PHP2Shell, says PHP powers 70% of websites, including WordPress, Drupal, and Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, that every PHP version back to 5.4 is hit by at least one flaw, and that proving the flaws could be exploited took a chain of steps “at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve” until frontier models lowered that barrier. Wiz says it confirmed working attacks against Drupal and WordPress in August before reporting to PHP. OpenAI calls it “one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” released a PHP version checker as a Codex skill, and committed $1 billion in subsidized access to its security tools for defenders with limited resources. PHP 8.1 and older no longer get official updates.

title: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, an agent that comes to you first, sends a morning brief, and asks before it acts
summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent, by waitlist for U.S. Pro and Max subscribers. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief on the most important items across your connected apps, checks those accounts every few hours, and messages you only when something needs attention. It has its own virtual machine and browser, so it keeps working when your laptop or phone is off. Before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for approval, and some things, like trading securities or moving money between accounts, are off-limits even with approval. A new classifier blocks it from sharing credit card numbers and government ID. Anthropic says this early version may still misread a thread or misjudge what’s urgent, and it shares usage limits with the rest of Claude.

title: AI doubts are back: the Nasdaq drops 2.6% and the S&P 500 has its worst day since July
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled on Thursday, October 22, as a batch of high-profile earnings reports revived fears about the AI spending race, Reuters reports. The S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.60% to 26,008.86, its steepest daily drop since early June, while the Dow eked out a 0.02% gain to 52,867.98. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index plunged 6.7%, its biggest one-day drop since June 23, and Intel, AMD, Sandisk, and Marvell each fell more than 8%. The weakness was concentrated: the AP notes most U.S. stocks actually rose, and Procter & Gamble, Lockheed Martin, Blackstone, and Spotify all gained after their reports. Oil hit its highest level since May, according to the AP.

title: Meta beat forecasts but slid 7% after its first cash outflow in more than a decade
summary: Meta Platforms’ third-quarter results beat analyst expectations, but its stock fell 7.0% on Thursday, October 22, Reuters reports, as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade because of its AI spending. Meta’s own release showed negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion on record revenue of $64.60 billion. Investors also weighed Meta’s plan to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise money for AI, which Meta’s release describes as a new Class C common stock to be issued as a stock dividend. CNBC reported that Meta was lower again in early trading on Friday.

title: Jensen Huang says neocloud demand is “off the charts” but capital is scarce, as Nvidia falls 4.4%
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on Thursday, October 22, at Nvidia’s GTC conference in Berlin, that demand for neocloud companies, which rent out AI computing, is “off the charts,” but scarce capital is holding back growth. “The demand of the capital is much greater than the availability of the capital. That’s going to get solved,” he said, adding that Europe will need “a lot more neoclouds.” CNBC notes neocloud stocks such as CoreWeave and Nebius have been selling off on worries about AI infrastructure spending and debt, and that Nvidia has committed nearly $10 billion to European companies, universities, and research institutions. In Thursday’s chip selloff, Nvidia shares dropped 4.4%, CNBC reported, and were rebounding slightly in early Friday trading.

title: Recursive releases Flint, a free coding model that runs on a laptop and that it says was largely built by AI
summary: Recursive, the startup led by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, released its first model, Flint, on October 21, TechCrunch reports. It’s a mixture-of-experts coding model that uses 2.5 billion of its 40 billion parameters at a time, light enough for an ordinary laptop, and it’s free on Hugging Face under the open Apache 2.0 license. In Recursive’s tests it generated about 131 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, roughly twice similar models, beat other models under 50 billion parameters on SWE-Bench Verified, and trailed only Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B on Recursive’s six-test average. Recursive says its automated research system, the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step, including low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality, letting a small team build it from scratch in under four months. The company says Flint needs more guidance than big paid coding assistants and suggests breaking large tasks into smaller steps.

title: Inception’s Mercury 3 writes like a diffusion image model, refining whole drafts at over 1,000 tokens a second
summary: Inception released Mercury 3 on October 19, calling it the most capable diffusion-based language model to date. Instead of writing one word at a time, a diffusion model refines a whole draft in parallel passes. Inception says Mercury 3 matches or beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 across a range of benchmarks while running 4 to 8 times faster, at 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs, with a 1-million-token context window, up from 260,000 for Mercury 2.5. It is more than 40 times larger than Mercury 1. Regular pricing is $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.70 per million output, half off at launch, and it’s available on Inception’s platform, OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel. Early users include support, tutoring, and web-navigation companies; one partner, TinyFish AI, says Mercury 3 completed 50% of 50 live web-navigation tasks.

title: iFlytek launches Spark X2.6, a 1-million-token model it says was trained entirely on Chinese chips
summary: At its developer festival in Beijing on October 22, iFlytek launched Spark X2.6, a mixture-of-experts model with 293 billion total and about 30 billion active parameters and a 1-million-token context window, aimed at coding and agent tasks, AGI Pulse reports. iFlytek says it was trained entirely on Chinese-made computing hardware, and chairman Liu Qingfeng claimed Spark is the only mainstream Chinese model not trained on NVIDIA GPUs. Launch pricing, 40% off, is ¥0.9 per million input tokens and ¥3.6 per million output, about $0.13 and $0.51. The flagship’s weights are closed, but a smaller sibling, Spark-X2.6-4B, is open under Apache 2.0 with the same 1-million-token context. iFlytek gave no benchmark scores for the flagship.

title: Hugging Face’s Carbon-X lets researchers chat with DNA, and it runs on a laptop
summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X on Thursday, October 22, an open model trained on both genomic sequences and natural language so people can ask questions about how DNA changes affect gene activity and health and get conversational answers, Wired reports. It was built with researchers at Zhongguancun Academy in China and the University of Naples Federico II in Italy. The team taught an existing language model to read DNA in six-letter chunks and trained it on 300 billion tokens mixing DNA from mammals, plants, fungi, and more with English text, deliberately leaving out viruses to avoid dangerous uses. At 14 billion parameters it can run on a user’s own hardware, so sensitive patient data doesn’t have to leave the lab. It reads stretches of about 50,000 DNA letters at a time, not whole genomes. “We’ve unlocked a new capability in language models, which is fundamentally about being able to chat with DNA,” said Hugging Face’s Lewis Tunstall.

title: Rivals team up: OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex are coming to Google Cloud
summary: OpenAI and Google Cloud announced on October 21 that OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud’s Model Garden, paired with Google Cloud’s access controls and data governance. Customers will buy the models through the Google Cloud Marketplace and can count the purchases against their existing Google Cloud spending commitments. OpenAI says its models will also soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent. “We are focused on giving customers a broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI,” said Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian. General availability is planned in the coming weeks, and OpenAI notes that Microsoft remains its primary cloud partner.

title: Use your head start: the PHP fix shows what happens when the good guys get there first
summary: OpenAI says that, to its knowledge, frontier AI found the PHP flaws before attackers did, opening what it calls a “Defender’s Window” for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections before going public. Wiz reported the bugs in August, and PHP took two months to build and verify a coordinated fix. The lesson for any project: when you spot a problem early, spend the head start on preparation, not panic. And the most useful thing you can do today might be as simple as checking that your tools are up to date.

title: Break the boulder into steps: a small team built a model from scratch in under four months
summary: Recursive says a small team, helped by its automated research system, built Flint from scratch in under four months, and its own advice for using Flint is to break large tasks into smaller steps. That advice works for people too. A big goal feels impossible as one leap but doable as a staircase: pick the next step, finish it, check it, and climb again. Gather the data, do the work, juice the brain.

title: Today at lunch: free Bach Lunch with Lafayette singer-songwriter Amelie Cecile in Parc Sans Souci
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s free lunchtime concert series is in Parc Sans Souci, 201 E. Vermilion St., today, Friday, October 23. Food vendors start selling at 11 a.m. and Lafayette singer-songwriter Amelie Cecile plays from noon to 1 p.m. with her four-piece band; she writes all her own songs, blending acoustic warmth with modern folk storytelling. Bring blankets and chairs and eat picnic-style.

title: Tonight at 6: Alliance Française screens “Fanon” in French with English subtitles
summary: Alliance Française de Lafayette’s Cine Club shows “Fanon” tonight, Friday, October 23, from 6 to 8 p.m. at 735 Jefferson St. The film follows Frantz Fanon after he’s appointed chief medical officer at the psychiatric hospital in Blida, Algeria, where his humane methods anger his colleagues as the Algerian independence struggle grows. It’s in French with English subtitles, with a presentation by Bhynty Charif and a friendly discussion afterward. It’s free for members and $5 for non-members, drink and snack included; RSVP by 5 p.m. today.

title: Tonight at 7:30: “Where the Suga Still Sweet,” a play by Breaux Bridge native Brian Egland, at the AcA
summary: Black Theater Experience presents “Where the Suga Still Sweet,” written by Breaux Bridge native Brian Egland, at the Acadiana Center for the Arts’ James Devin Moncus Theater, 101 W. Vermilion St., tonight, Friday, October 23, at 7:30 p.m. In a field of cane that won’t grow right, one patch does: it’s where Sondelo is buried, and where his best friend Runna goes to talk to him. Tickets are $35, according to the AcA.

title: Tonight at 8: Zach Top brings the Cold Beer & Country Music Tour to the Cajundome, with Lukas Nelson
summary: Country singer Zach Top plays the Lafayette Cajundome tonight, Friday, October 23, at 8 p.m. on his Cold Beer & Country Music Tour 2026, with Lukas Nelson also on the bill, according to Live Nation’s listing. Tickets are sold through Live Nation.

title: Saturday: Boo Bayou Family Fall Fest at Vermilionville, with trick-or-treating and a petting zoo
summary: Vermilionville, 300 Fisher Road, hosts its Boo Bayou Family Fall Fest on Saturday, October 24, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Activities include trick-or-treating, games, crafts, face painting, a petting zoo, juggling, and vendor booths. Admission is $5 for guests 2 and older, according to the Bayou Vermilion District listing.

title: Saturday: a 100-vendor card show at the Heymann Center and the free Creole Rendezvous at Heymann Park
summary: Saturday, October 24, starts at 9 a.m. with the Acadiana Card Show at the Heymann Center, with more than 100 vendors of sports cards, Pokémon, trading card games, and collectibles, according to Acadiana Profile. At 1 p.m., the African American Heritage Foundation hosts Creole Rendezvous, a free annual celebration of Louisiana’s Creole culture and heritage at Heymann Park, 1500 S. Orange St., with live zydeco from The Creole Connection and a marketplace of local vendors and farmers, according to Zydeco Events.
